{{nihongo|'''Mifune Shrine'''|御船神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

**Mifune Shrine** (みふねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=subsidiary shrine}} of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). This article also describes **Mumino Shrine** (むみのじんじゃ), which is enshrined at the same site as Mifune Shrine.
Both are shrines that enshrine {{ill|Suijin|Q3137449|qid=Q3137449|lt=river gods}}.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunkasha, ed. (2008): p. 64</ref>
=== Overview ===
This section describes matters common to both shrines.
They are located in Toba (pronounced *Toba* or *Doba*), {{ill|Taki, Mie|Q1203963|qid=Q1203963}}, {{ill|Taki District, Mie|Q1042360|qid=Q1042360}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}.<ref name="sk8">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 378</ref> The local {{ill|Toponym|Q7884789|qid=Q7884789}} “Toba” means “stopping place,” and is said to derive from the tradition that the boat of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}} once stopped there.<ref name="tc5">Kaneko (1983): p. 55</ref>
The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine buildings}} are constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545}} style and are surrounded by a {{ill|Sacred fences|Q3078312|qid=Q3078312}} fence. There is no {{ill|Saisen|Q988479|qid=Q988479}}. A {{ill|Nightlight|Q762277|qid=Q762277}} stands at the entrance to the shrine grounds.<ref name="ic"/> The total {{ill|Area|Q11500|qid=Q11500}} of the grounds is 975 {{ill|Pyeong|Q706688|qid=Q706688}} (approximately 3,223 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}).<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 380</ref>
=== Mifune Shrine ===
Mifune Shrine ranks 24th among the 27 subsidiary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11</ref> It is said to be a shrine established by Yamatohime-no-Mikoto when she moored her boat during her journey up the Tokida River (Outer Tokida River).<ref name="ic"/> She stopped here because the river narrowed and boats could no longer pass.<ref name="tc5"/>
In the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, it is recorded as “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine.”<ref name="sk8"/> “Ōkami no Mifune” is thought to mean the boat upon which {{ill|Amaterasu|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}} rode. Sonoda Moriyoshi suggested that after the transfer of the deity, the boat container (*mifunashiro*) holding the sacred casket (*mihishiro*) that enshrined the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} of Amaterasu Ōmikami may have been placed at Mifune Shrine.<ref name="sk8"/>
The enshrined deity is Ōkami no Mikagekawa no Kami.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 68</ref> This deity is regarded either as the {{ill|Guardian deities|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957}} of the Tokida River, which irrigates the surrounding fields,<ref name="ic"/> or as a guardian deity of waterborne transportation.<ref name="gk"/> The same {{ill|Kami|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=deity}} is also enshrined at {{ill|Kano Shrine|Q17225745|qid=Q17225745}}, another subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 59</ref> The term “Mikage” carries meanings of {{ill|Soul|Q9165|qid=Q9165}} and blessing (“okage”), and according to *Jingū Tenryaku*, it refers to the spirit of a great deity enshrined by the river that supplies water to the {{ill|Shinden (divine field)|Q10855080|qid=Q10855080}}.<ref name="sk9">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 379</ref>
There are alternative theories regarding the enshrined deity: *Ise Nisho Daijingū Shinmei Hisho* records it as “Ōkami no Mifune no Kami,” *Engishiki Jinmyōchō Hian-shū* as “Ame-no-Torifune no Kami,” and *Ise no Kuni Jinmyōchō Kōshō* as “Toriishikusufune no Kami.”<ref name="sk0"/>
=== Mumino Shrine ===
Mumino Shrine ranks 15th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall, ed. (1929): pp. 13–14</ref> Its shrine building was discontinued, and it is now enshrined together with Mifune Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall, ed. (1929): p. 14</ref>
The enshrined deities are Samukawahiko no Mikoto and Samukawahime no Mikoto.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> They are guardian deities of the Tokida River<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> and are said to be children of Ōminakami no Mikoto.<ref name="gk"/> “Samukawa,” the name of the deities, is an alternate name for the Tokida River, and is said to have been given by Yamatohime-no-Mikoto because the river’s water was cold.<ref name="tc5"/>
=== History ===
By definition, as a subsidiary shrine of Ise Grand Shrine, Mifune Shrine must have been founded before the compilation of the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, that is, before {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}).<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 22</ref> The *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō* records the phrase “designated and celebrated by Princess Yamatohime.”<ref name="sk8"/> Since it appears in this text, the shrine is considered to have existed before {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|804|Q29998|qid=Q29998}}).<ref name="ic2"/>
In {{ill|Ancient history|Q41493|qid=Q41493}}, Toba belonged to Tanabe-go of {{ill|Watarai District|ceb|Watarai-gun|ckb|گەڕەکی واتاری|es|Distrito de Watarai|fr|District de Watarai|id|Distrik Watarai, Mie|it|Distretto di Watarai|ja|度会郡|ko|와타라이군|pl|Powiat Watarai|uk|Повіт Ватарай|zh|度會郡|qid=Q1131032}}, but in {{ill|Taika (era)|Q1077930|qid=Q1077930}} 5 ({{ill|649|Q31117|qid=Q31117}}), Taki District was separated from Watarai District, and the area came to belong to Ari-go of Taki District.<ref name="tc5"/> Because of this history, the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* lists “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine” under Watarai District.<ref name="sk9"/>
From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} onward, rituals were discontinued, but on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 3, {{ill|August 29 (Lunisolar)|Q840048|qid=Q840048}} ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138}}: {{ill|1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577}} {{ill|September 30|Q2881|qid=Q2881}}), the shrine was reestablished at its present site.<ref name="sk8"/> At that time, remains of moats, old post holes, and decayed wood were discovered, leading the site to be regarded as the former shrine location.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 378–379</ref> {{ill|Mikannagi Kiyonao|Q6537624|qid=Q6537624}} supported this identification, while Nakagawa Tsunemasa argued that the former site was a local {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} shrine in a neighboring village, colloquially called “Mifune-sha.”<ref name="sk9"/> In {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 14 ({{ill|1843|Q7629|qid=Q7629}}), a stone lantern was installed at the shrine entrance.<ref name="gk"/>
In {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), Mumino Shrine, whose location had been unknown since the medieval period, was enshrined together with Mifune Shrine.<ref name="sk0"/>
=== Access ===
;Public transportation
* About a 17-minute walk (approximately 900 m) from {{ill|Tokida Station|Q7813584|qid=Q7813584}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}} of {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679}}.<ref name="ic-P63">Ise Bunkasha, ed. (2008): p. 63</ref> Walk along the {{ill|Miyagawa irrigation canal|Q11454721|qid=Q11454721}} from the south side of Tokida Station; the elevated ground on the right is Mifune Shrine / Mumino Shrine.<ref name="ic"/>
;By car
* About 14 minutes (approximately 5.9 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km}}) from {{ill|Tamaki interchange|Q11572465|qid=Q11572465|lt=Tamaki IC}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|Q6079578|qid=Q6079578}}. There is no {{ill|Parking lot|Q6501349|qid=Q6501349}} nearby.

'''Mifune Shrine''' (みふねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=subsidiary shrine}} of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|abstract|Q11581011|ja|皇大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Naku|zh|皇大神宮|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). This article also describes '''Mumino Shrine''' (むみのじんじゃ), which is enshrined at the same site as Mifune Shrine.
Both are shrines that enshrine {{ill|Suijin|Q3137449|qid=Q3137449|lt=river gods}}.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p.64</ref>
=== Overview ===
This section describes matters common to both shrines.
They are located in Toba (read as Toba or Doba), {{ill|Taki, Mie|Q1203963|qid=Q1203963}}, {{ill|Taki District, Mie|Q1042360|qid=Q1042360}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}.<ref name="sk8">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p.378</ref> The place name “Toba” means “stopping place,” and is said to derive from the fact that the boat of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}} stopped there.<ref name="tc5">Kaneko (1983): p.55</ref>
The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine buildings}} are constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545}} style and are surrounded by a {{ill|Sacred fences|Q3078312|qid=Q3078312}} fence. No {{ill|Saisen|Q988479|qid=Q988479}} is placed. At the entrance to the shrine grounds stands a {{ill|Nightlight|Q762277|qid=Q762277}}.<ref name="ic"/> The area of the shrine grounds is 975 {{ill|Pyeong|Q706688|qid=Q706688}} (approximately 3,223 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}).<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p.380</ref>
=== Mifune Shrine ===
Mifune Shrine ranks 24th among the 27 subsidiary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp.9–11</ref> It is a shrine established at a place where Yamatohime-no-mikoto moored her boat during her journey upstream along the Tokida River.<ref name="ic"/> She stopped here because the river became too narrow for boats to pass.<ref name="tc5"/>
In the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, it is recorded as “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine.”<ref name="sk8"/> “Ōkami no Mifune” is thought to mean the boat on which {{ill|Amaterasu|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}} rides, and Sonoda Moriyoshi conjectured that the vessel (mifunashiro) containing the sacred container for the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} of Amaterasu Ōmikami was placed at Mifune Shrine after the transfer of the deity.<ref name="sk8"/>
The enshrined deity is Ōkami no Mikagekawa no Kami.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.68</ref> This deity is regarded as the {{ill|Guardian deities|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957}} of the Tokida River, which irrigates fields,<ref name="ic"/> or as a guardian deity of water transportation.<ref name="gk"/> The same {{ill|Kami|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=deity}} is also enshrined at {{ill|Kano Shrine|Q17225745|qid=Q17225745}}, another subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Kaneko (1983): p.59</ref> “Mikage” carries meanings of {{ill|Soul|Q9165|qid=Q9165}} and blessing (“okage”), and *Jingū Tenryaku* explains it as the spirit of the great deity enshrined beside the river that draws water to the {{ill|Shinden (divine field)|Q10855080|qid=Q10855080}}.<ref name="sk9">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p.379</ref>
There are alternative theories regarding the enshrined deity: *Ise Nishō Daijingū Shinmei Hisho* gives “Ōkami no Mifune no Kami,” *Engishiki Jinmyōchō Hian-shū* gives “Ame no Torifune no Kami,” and *Ise no Kuni Jinmyōchō Kōshō* gives “Toriishi Kusufune no Kami.”<ref name="sk0"/>
=== Mumino Shrine ===
Mumino Shrine ranks 15th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp.13–14</ref> Its shrine building was discontinued, and it is enshrined together with Mifune Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p.14</ref>
The enshrined deities are Samukawahiko no Mikoto and Samukawahime no Mikoto.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> They are guardian deities of the Tokida River<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> and children of Ōminakami no Mikoto.<ref name="gk"/> “Samukawa,” the name of the deities, is an alternate name for the Tokida River, said to have been given by Yamatohime-no-mikoto because the river water was cold.<ref name="tc5"/>
=== History ===
By definition as a subsidiary shrine of Ise Grand Shrine, Mifune Shrine must have been founded before the compilation of the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}).<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref> The *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō* records “Yamatohime Naishinnō Sadame-iwai.”<ref name="sk8"/> Since it is mentioned in the *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō*, it is considered to have existed before the 23rd year of {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} ({{ill|804|Q29998|qid=Q29998}}).<ref name="ic2"/>
In {{ill|Ancient history|Q41493|qid=Q41493}}, Toba belonged to Tanabe-go of {{ill|Watarai District|ceb|Watarai-gun|ckb|گەڕەکی واتاری|es|Distrito de Watarai|fr|District de Watarai|id|Distrik Watarai, Mie|it|Distretto di Watarai|ja|度会郡|ko|와타라이군|pl|Powiat Watarai|uk|Повіт Ватарай|zh|度會郡|qid=Q1131032}}, but in the 5th year of {{ill|Taika (era)|Q1077930|qid=Q1077930}} ({{ill|649|Q31117|qid=Q31117}}), Taki District was separated from Watarai District, and the area came to belong to Uni-go of Taki District.<ref name="tc5"/> Because of this history, the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* lists “Ōkami no Mifune Shrine” under Watarai District.<ref name="sk9"/>
From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} onward, rituals ceased, but the shrine was revived at its present location on the 29th day of the 8th month of the 3rd year of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} ({{ill|Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138}}: September 30, {{ill|1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577}}).<ref name="sk8"/> At that time, traces of a {{ill|Moat|Q88480|qid=Q88480}}, old post holes, and decayed wood were discovered, leading the site to be considered the former shrine location.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp.378–379</ref> {{ill|Mikannagi Kiyonao|Q6537624|qid=Q6537624}} supported this theory, while Nakagawa Tsunemasa argued that a {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} shrine in a neighboring village, colloquially called “Mifune-sha” by locals, was the former site.<ref name="sk9"/> In the 14th year of {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} ({{ill|1843|Q7629|qid=Q7629}}), a stone lantern was installed at the shrine entrance.<ref name="gk"/>
In {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), Mumino Shrine, whose location had been unknown since the medieval period, was enshrined together with Mifune Shrine.<ref name="sk0"/>
=== Access ===
;Public transportation
* About a 17-minute walk (approximately 900 m) from {{ill|Tokida Station|Q7813584|qid=Q7813584}} on the {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679}} {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}}.<ref name="ic-P63">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p.63</ref> Walk along the {{ill|Miyagawa Irrigation Canal|Q11454721|qid=Q11454721}} from the front (south) side of Tokida Station; the elevated ground visible on the right is Mifune Shrine / Mumino Shrine.<ref name="ic"/>
;By car
* About 14 minutes (approximately 5.9 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km}}) from {{ill|Tamaki interchange|Q11572465|qid=Q11572465|lt=Tamaki IC}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|Q6079578|qid=Q6079578}}. There is no {{ill|Parking lot|Q6501349|qid=Q6501349}} nearby.
